Let \(A,B,C,D\) be position vectors. Since each new point lies beyond the endpoint with equal length,  
\[
B'=2B-A,\quad C'=2C-B,\quad D'=2D-C,\quad A'=2A-D.
\]
Using the shoelace formula for oriented double area \(S\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
S(A'B'C'D') &= (2A-D)\times(2B-A)+(2B-A)\times(2C-B)\\
&\quad +(2C-B)\times(2D-C)+(2D-C)\times(2A-D).
\end{aligned}
\]

Expanding and canceling cross terms gives
\[
S(A'B'C'D')=5\bigl(A\times B+B\times C+C\times D+D\times A\bigr)=5S(ABCD).
\]
Thus the new area is \(5\cdot 10=50\).

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
